A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same research work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-G. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original checkpoint evaluations, crosscoder reconstruction results, feature-ablation experiments, and linguistic feature analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including reconstruction statistics in Appendix D and RELIE-versus-RELDEC ablation results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The crosscoder architecture, training objective, checkpoint-selection procedure, integrated-gradient attribution, and two-way and three-way RELIE computations remain unchanged. Added explanations do not introduce method components.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Pile, Dolma, and mC4 training samples and BLiMP, MultiBLiMP, and CLAMS evaluations. The languages, agreement subtasks, and checkpoint scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: RELDEC remains the comparator to RELIE in Appendix E and Table 7. The additional attribution-method citation in v2 does not correspond to a newly evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Checkpoint selections, middle layers, dataset sampling, 400M-token training budgets, evaluation metrics, ten-step integrated gradients, and IE thresholds are unchanged. The revised layer-selection discussion explains the existing setting.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same feature-ablation correlation study, pairwise-versus-triplet analyses, annotation case studies, and supplementary feature-evolution and crosslingual-overlap analyses in Appendices E-G.

E5.justification: Both report the same three training seeds, 124, 153, and 6582, and average crosscoder statistics over them. No uncertainty intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run reporting practices are added or revised.

E6.justification: Empirical plots, numerical tables, and feature annotations retain their results. Table 7 preserves overall RELIE correlations of 0.945 and 0.952 versus RELDEC's 0.787 and 0.843. The reconstruction statistics are unchanged despite moving from Table 4 to Table 6.

T1.justification: Equations 1-11 and the mathematical definitions remain unchanged. Appendix F.1 adds motivation for integrated gradients, without introducing a theorem, proof, assumption, or revised derivation.

C1.justification: Both retain the claims of tracking feature emergence, persistence, and disappearance, progression toward linguistic abstractions, and crosslingual consolidation. The revised conclusion explicitly restates RELIE's contribution already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds rationales for comparing checkpoints within one training run, selecting middle layers, using controlled minimal pairs, and choosing integrated gradients. It also softens the early-checkpoint limitation by removing the assertion that a more-trained model is generally needed.

D1.justification: Hyperparameters, hardware, training times, preprocessing, annotation instructions, and resource links are retained. Section 5's explicit middle-block output description restates information already documented in v1's Appendices C-D.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kramár et al. (2024) to motivate attribution choices and replaces Liu et al. (2019) with Liu and Niehues (2025) in the layer-selection rationale. The broader positioning relative to interpretability and training-dynamics research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites improve the abstract, motivation, layer and benchmark explanations, conclusion, and appendix prose. Acknowledgments are updated, while the section hierarchy and most text remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1's illustrative panel is lightly redrawn, captions and the heatmap-scale explanation are refined, and Figure 3 moves from page 5 to page 6. Appendix Tables 4-6 are reordered and renumbered; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the unchanged study easier to understand through clearer explanations of checkpoint comparability, layer selection, benchmark suitability, and integrated gradients. The early-checkpoint caveat is slightly softened, but its central warning remains. These are modest clarity gains; the empirical support and technical contributions are unchanged.
